Make a final call to direct_pte_prefetch_many() if there are ""trailing""
SPTEs to prefetch
column2: i.e. SPTEs for GFNs following the faulting GFN.  The

column1: call to direct_pte_prefetch_many() in the loop only handles the case
where there are !PRESENT SPTEs preceding a PRESENT SPTE.
E.g. if the faulting GFN is a multiple of 8 (the prefetch size) and all
SPTEs for the following GFNs are !PRESENT
start = sptep+1"" and not prefetch any SPTEs.
Prefetching trailing SPTEs as intended can drastically reduce the number
of guest page faults
column2: e.g. accessing the first byte of every 4kb page in

column1: a 6gb chunk of virtual memory
column2: in a VM with 8gb of preallocated memory

column1: the number of pf_fixed events observed in L0 drops from ~1.75M to <0.27M.
Note
column2: this only affects memory that is backed by 4kb pages as KVM doesn't

column1: prefetch when installing hugepages.  Shadow paging prefetching is not
affected as it does not batch the prefetches due to the need to process
the corresponding guest PTE.  The TDP MMU is not affected because it
doesn't have prefetching
